title: Prescribed Burn Approval Act of 2016
official_summary:
Prescribed Burn Approval Act of 2016

This bill prohibits the Forest Service from authorizing a prescribed burn (i.e., a planned fire intentionally ignited) on Forest Service land if, for the county or contiguous county in which such land is located, the national fire danger rating system is indicating an extreme fire danger level.

Nonetheless, the Forest Service may authorize a prescribed burn under such a condition if it coordinates with the applicable state government and local fire officials.

summary.headline: A 2016 law bars the Forest Service from approving planned controlled burns on its land when fire danger is rated extreme in that county or a neighboring county, unless it coordinates with state and local officials.
summary.what_it_does: The law stops the Forest Service from authorizing a prescribed burn, which is a planned fire set on purpose, on Forest Service land when the national fire danger rating system shows an extreme danger level for that county or a contiguous county. The agency may still approve a burn under those conditions if it coordinates with the applicable state government and local fire officials. The summary does not describe other requirements or procedures.

who_it_affects.how: It cannot approve prescribed burns on its land during extreme fire danger unless it first coordinates with state and local officials.

who_it_affects.group: State governments and local fire officials
who_it_affects.how: They become part of the required coordination when the Forest Service wants to approve a burn during extreme fire danger.

who_it_affects.group: People living near Forest Service land in counties with extreme fire danger ratings
who_it_affects.how: Planned burns on nearby federal land are restricted during those conditions unless officials coordinate on the decision.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 14, 2016, and the official summary does not state a separate effective date.
